title: Idempotents lift uniquely along a base change of a nilpotent thickening
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $J\subseteq A$ an ideal with $J^N=0$ for some $N\ge1$, $g:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $Y_0=Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)$ the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] and $i:Y_0\to Y$ the first projection. Then (1) $i$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] whose quasi-coherent ideal sheaf $\mathcal J=\ker(\mathcal O_Y\to i_*\mathcal O_{Y_0})$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] satisfies $\mathcal J^N=0$ [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers], so $Y$ is a finite order thickening of $Y_0$ and $i$ is a homeomorphism of underlying topological spaces [def-sbc-first-order-thickening]; (2) the ring map $i^\sharp:\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)\to\Gamma(Y_0,\mathcal O_{Y_0})$ induces a bijection from the set of idempotents of $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ to the set of idempotents of $\Gamma(Y_0,\mathcal O_{Y_0})$: every idempotent of $\Gamma(Y_0,\mathcal O_{Y_0})$ is $i^\sharp(e)$ for exactly one idempotent $e\in\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma Tag 09ZU (lemma-base-change-thickening, line 209; proof omitted) with Definition Tag 04EX (definition-thickening, line 36) for (1); (2) is the step of Derived Categories, proof of Lemma Tag 0G7X (perfect.tex lines 8137-8146: 'Since the underlying topological space of X_n is equal to that of X_s we obtain ... a nontrivial idempotent e_n'), via idempotents <-> open and closed subsets (Algebra, Lemma Tag 00EE)

proof.text: *Step 1 ($i$ is a closed immersion with ideal $J\mathcal O_Y$).* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-base-change-closed-immersion-ideal] with $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $X=Y$, $f=g$ and $K=J$: then $X_K=Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)=Y_0$ and $j_K$ is the first projection $i$. By its part (1), $i$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] whose ideal sheaf $\mathcal J=\ker(\mathcal O_Y\to i_*\mathcal O_{Y_0})$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] is $J\mathcal O_Y$, and for every affine open $U\subseteq Y$ with $B=\mathcal O_Y(U)$ (an $A$-algebra via $g$) one has $\mathcal J(U)=JB$, the ideal of $B$ generated by the image of $J$, with $i^{-1}(U)\to U$ identified with $\operatorname{Spec}(B/JB)\to\operatorname{Spec}B$. (This is the closed-immersion part of Tag 09ZU: $\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)\subset\operatorname{Spec}A$ is a closed subscheme and its base change $Y_0\subset Y$ is one.)

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma Tag 09ZU (lemma-base-change-thickening, line 209; proof omitted), Definition Tag 04EX (definition-thickening, line 36)

proof.text: *Step 2 ($\mathcal J^N=0$; finite order thickening).* By part (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-base-change-closed-immersion-ideal] with $K=J$ and $m=N$, $\mathcal J^N=(J\mathcal O_Y)^N=J^N\mathcal O_Y$ (powers of quasi-coherent ideal sheaves [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers]). Since $J^N=0$, $J^N\mathcal O_Y$ is the image of $g^*\widetilde{0}=0$ in $\mathcal O_Y$, i.e. $\mathcal J^N=0$ (equivalently, on every affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $\mathcal J(U)^N=(JB)^N=J^NB=0$, a product of $N$ generators $a_1b_1\cdots a_Nb_N=(a_1\cdots a_N)b_1\cdots b_N$ with $a_k\in J$ lying in $J^NB$). With $n=N-1\ge0$ this says $\mathcal J^{n+1}=0$, so $Y$ is a finite order (indeed an $(N-1)$st order) thickening of $Y_0$ in the sense of [def-sbc-first-order-thickening] (3), once Step 3 shows the underlying spaces agree (part (1) of that definition).

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma Tag 09ZU (lemma-base-change-thickening, line 209; proof omitted), Definition Tag 04EX (definition-thickening, line 36)

proof.text: Step 3 (homeomorphism). Since N >= 1, Mathlib Scheme.IdealSheafData.support_pow gives support(i.ker^N) = support(i.ker). The power is zero by Step 2 and Scheme.IdealSheafData.support_bot gives full support. Scheme.Hom.support_ker identifies this support with the closure of the image of i (closed immersions are quasi-compact). The image of a closed immersion is closed, so closure(image i) = image i, and i is surjective. Apply isHomeomorph_iff_isEmbedding_surjective to its closed embedding. This replaces the affine prime-by-prime argument using lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-image-zero-locus by the existing Mathlib support API; it is precisely the same argument packaged by Mathlib.

proof.text: *Step 4 (idempotents, statement (2)).* For a scheme $X$ let $\mathrm{Idem}(X)$ be the set of idempotents of $\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$, $\mathrm{Clop}(X)$ the set of open and closed subsets of $X$, and $\beta_X:\mathrm{Idem}(X)\to\mathrm{Clop}(X)$, $e\mapsto U_e=\{x:e_x\neq0\}$, a bijection by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-clopen-idempotent] (b) (the scheme form of Algebra 00EE). By part (c) of that lemma applied to $i:Y_0\to Y$, for $e\in\mathrm{Idem}(Y)$ the section $i^\sharp(e)$ is idempotent and $\beta_{Y_0}(i^\sharp e)=i^{-1}(\beta_Y(e))$. Since $i$ is a homeomorphism (Step 3), $U\mapsto i^{-1}(U)$ is a bijection $\mathrm{Clop}(Y)\to\mathrm{Clop}(Y_0)$ (inverse $V\mapsto i(V)$). Hence the restriction of $i^\sharp$ to $\mathrm{Idem}(Y)$ equals $\beta_{Y_0}^{-1}\circ i^{-1}\circ\beta_Y$, a composite of three bijections, so it is a bijection $\mathrm{Idem}(Y)\to\mathrm{Idem}(Y_0)$: every idempotent of $\Gamma(Y_0,\mathcal O_{Y_0})$ is $i^\sharp(e)$ for exactly one idempotent $e$ of $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$, namely $e=\beta_Y^{-1}(i(U_{e_0}))$ for the given $e_0$. (This is the step of the proof of Tag 0G7X: the decomposition $X_s=T_1\amalg T_2$ given by $e$ is a decomposition of the equal underlying space of $X_n$, giving the idempotent $e_n$.)

lean.statement: theorem nilpotent_baseChange_idempotents (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (J : Ideal A) (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (hJ : J ^ N = ⊥) (Y : Scheme.{u}) (g : Y ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) : let q := Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk J)) let Y₀ := pullback g q let i : Y₀ ⟶ Y := pullback.fst g q IsClosedImmersion i ∧ i.ker ^ N = ⊥ ∧ IsFiniteOrderThickening i ∧ IsHomeomorph i ∧ (∀ e₀ : Γ(Y₀, ⊤), IsIdempotentElem e₀ → ∃! e : {e : Γ(Y, ⊤) // IsIdempotentElem e}, (Scheme.Γ.map i.op).hom e.val = e₀)
